title: Review: DO_KDF HKDF/PBKDF2 implementation (ae9d714, 179f504)
notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — five P1 issues (two API contract bugs, two FIPS compliance gaps, one footgun), no P0 memory safety or crash bugs. Code is functionally correct: no double-unlock, no double-free, copy_from_user/fget/fput all paired correctly, IKM always zeroized. Risk comes from FIPS compliance gaps (PBKDF2 salt, key purpose binding) that will generate audit findings.
Confidence: 25% chance of a missed bug. Uncertainty driven by: (1) kernel hkdf_extract() NULL-salt behavior — the code passes NULL when salt_len==0, mirroring fs/crypto/hkdf.c, but the kernel HKDF API is lightly documented and this pattern is not in the tests yet; (2) wolfCrypt wc_PBKDF2 behavior with edge inputs (passwd_len == inbuf_len which could be up to CRYPTO2DEV_KEY_IMPORT_MAXLEN=8192 — cast to int, no overflow check); (3) FIPS 140-3 boundary compliance of the ikm_fd==-1 enforcement path. Would raise confidence if: full test coverage of HKDF with zero-salt on a running kernel, PBKDF2 with passwd_len > 32767 (int overflow on cast), and FIPS module boundary review by a CMVP consultant.
